overview: This House resolution holds Leon D. Black in contempt of Congress for not complying with two subpoenas, legal orders to testify and to hand over documents, that the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform issued to him on June 26, 2026. One subpoena required him to sit for a deposition (questioning under oath) and the other required him to produce documents. The resolution directs the Speaker of the House to send the committee's report to the U.S. Attorney for the District of Columbia, the federal prosecutor who can decide whether to bring criminal charges under the federal contempt-of-Congress law. It also tells the Speaker to take any other appropriate steps to enforce the subpoenas. As of September 16, 2026, the House had adopted it.
for: Supporters say Congress cannot carry out its investigations if people can ignore subpoenas without consequence, and referring the matter to prosecutors is the step the law provides.
against: Critics say contempt referrals can be a heavy-handed tool against a private citizen, and disputes over the scope of a subpoena are better worked out through negotiation or the courts.
